sourceDate.text: 王建以為武信軍節度使

units.zh: 劉知俊
units.en: Liu Zhijun
units.literal: Liu Zhijun

units.zh: 劉知俊，字希賢，徐州沛人也。
units.en: Liu Zhijun, styled Xixian, came from Pei in Xuzhou.
units.literal: Liu Zhijun, courtesy name Xixian, was a native of Pei in Xuzhou.

units.zh: 少事時溥，溥與梁相攻，知俊與其麾下二千人降梁，太祖以為左開道指揮使。
units.en: As a youth he served Shi Pu. When Pu warred with Liang, Zhijun brought two thousand men over to Zhu Wen, who made him commander of the Left Vanguard detachment.
units.literal: In youth he served Shi Pu; when Pu fought Liang, Zhijun with two thousand men under his command surrendered to Liang, and the Founder made him commander of the Left Vanguard detachment.

units.zh: 知俊姿貌雄傑，能被甲上馬，輪劍入敵，勇出諸將。
units.en: He was a striking man—armored, mounted, sword in hand, he outfought every general in the host.
units.literal: Zhijun’s bearing was heroic; he could don armor and mount a horse, whirl a sword into the enemy ranks, and in courage surpassed the other generals.

units.zh: 當是時，劉開道名重軍中。
units.en: In those days the name Liu Kaidao carried great weight in camp.
units.literal: At that time the name Liu Kaidao weighed heavy in the army.

units.zh: 歷海、懷、鄭三州刺史，從破青州，以功表匡國軍節度使。
units.en: He held Hai, Huai, and Zheng in turn, helped take Qingzhou, and was named military governor of Kuangguo for his service.
units.literal: He successively served as prefect of Hai, Huai, and Zheng, followed in the capture of Qingzhou, and by merit was memorialized military governor of Kuangguo.

units.zh: 邠州楊崇本以兵六萬攻雍州，屯於美原。
units.en: Yang Chongben of Bin brought sixty thousand men against Yong and camped at Meiyuan.
units.literal: Yang Chongben of Binzhou led sixty thousand men against Yongzhou and encamped at Meiyuan.

units.zh: 是時，太祖方與諸將攻滄州，知俊不俟命，與康懷英等擊敗崇本，斬馘二萬，獲馬三千匹，執其偏裨百人。
units.en: The Founder was at Cangzhou with the main host. Zhijun did not wait for orders: with Kang Huaiying and others he smashed Chongben, took twenty thousand heads, three thousand horses, and a hundred officers prisoner.
units.literal: At that time the Founder was with the other generals attacking Cangzhou; Zhijun without awaiting orders joined Kang Huaiying and others, defeated Chongben, beheaded and counted twenty thousand heads, took three thousand horses, and seized a hundred of his officers.

units.zh: 李思安為夾城攻潞州，久不下，太祖罷思安，拜知俊行營招討使，未至潞，夾城已破，徙西路行營招討使，敗邠、岐兵於幕谷。
units.en: Li Si’an had Jiacheng on Luzhou and could not crack it. Zhu Wen replaced him with Zhijun as mobile-camp pacifier. Luzhou fell before Zhijun arrived; he was moved to the western route, beat Bin and Qi at Mugui.
units.literal: Li Si’an was besieging Luzhou at Jiacheng and could not take it; the Founder removed Si’an and made Zhijun mobile-camp pacification commissioner. Before he reached Luzhou, Jiacheng had fallen; he was shifted to western-route mobile-camp pacification commissioner and defeated Bin and Qi troops at Mugui.

units.zh: 是時，延州高萬興叛楊崇本降梁，太祖遣知俊會萬興，攻下丹、延、鄜、坊四州，加檢校太尉兼侍中，封大彭郡王。
units.en: Gao Wanxing of Yan broke from Chongben and came over to Liang. Zhu Wen sent Zhijun to join him; they took Dan, Yan, Fu, and Fang. Zhijun was made acting Grand Mentor and Palace Attendant and enfeoffed Prince of Dapeng.
units.literal: At that time Gao Wanxing of Yanzhou rebelled against Yang Chongben and surrendered to Liang; the Founder sent Zhijun to join Wanxing, took Dan, Yan, Bin, and Fang, and added him as acting Grand Mentor and Palace Attendant, enfeoffing him Prince of Dapeng commandery.

units.zh: 知俊功益高，太祖性多猜忌，屢殺諸將，王重師無罪見殺，知俊益懼，不自安。
units.en: Zhijun’s fame rose—and so did Zhu Wen’s suspicion. Generals died one after another; Wang Zhongshi was killed though innocent. Zhijun grew afraid and could not rest easy.
units.literal: As Zhijun’s merit grew higher, the Founder’s nature was much given to suspicion and he repeatedly killed generals; Wang Zhongshi was killed though guiltless, and Zhijun grew more afraid and ill at ease.

units.zh: 太祖已下鄜、坊，遣知俊復攻邠州，知俊以軍食不給未行。
units.en: Once Fu and Fang were his, the Founder ordered Zhijun back against Bin. Zhijun would not march: the army had no grain.
units.literal: After the Founder had taken Bin and Fang he sent Zhijun to attack Binzhou again, but Zhijun did not march because army provisions were lacking.

units.zh: 太祖幸河中，使宣徽使王殷召知俊。
units.en: The Founder went to Hezhong and sent Wang Yin of the Palace Secretariat to fetch Zhijun.
units.literal: The Founder visited Hezhong and sent Palace Secretariat commissioner Wang Yin to summon Zhijun.

units.zh: 其弟知浣為親軍指揮使，間遣人告知俊以不宜來。
units.en: His brother Zhihuan commanded the personal guard and sent word in secret: do not come.
units.literal: His younger brother Zhihuan was commander of the personal guard; he sent a man in secret to tell Zhijun he ought not to come.

units.zh: 知俊遂叛，臣於李茂貞，以兵攻雍、華，執劉捍送於鳳翔。
units.en: Zhijun rebelled, submitted to Li Maozhen, struck Yong and Hua, seized Liu Han, and sent him to Fengxiang.
units.literal: Zhijun then rebelled, submitted to Li Maozhen, and with troops attacked Yong and Hua, seizing Liu Han and sending him to Fengxiang.

units.zh: 太祖使人謂知俊曰：「朕待卿至矣，何相負邪？」
units.en: Zhu Wen sent word: “I have heaped favor on you—how can you betray me?”
units.literal: The Founder sent a man to say to Zhijun: “I have treated you to the utmost—how can you fail me?”

units.zh: 知俊報曰：「王重師不負陛下而族滅，臣非背德，但畏死爾！」
units.en: Zhijun answered: “Wang Zhongshi was loyal and his house was wiped out. I am not faithless—I am afraid to die!”
units.literal: Zhijun replied: “Wang Zhongshi did not fail Your Majesty yet his clan was exterminated; I am not ungrateful—I only fear death!”

units.zh: 太祖復使語曰：「朕固知卿以此，吾誅重師，乃劉捍誤我，致卿至此，吾豈不恨之邪？
units.en: Zhu Wen sent word again: “I knew why you fled. I killed Zhongshi because Liu Han misled me and drove you away—do you think I do not regret it?
units.literal: The Founder sent word again: “I always knew you acted from this. I executed Zhongshi because Liu Han misled me and brought you to this pass—do I not hate it?

units.zh: 今捍已死，未能塞責。」
units.en: Han is dead, and still I cannot make amends.”
units.literal: Han is already dead, yet I cannot answer for the fault.”

units.zh: 知俊不報，以兵斷潼關。
units.en: Zhijun made no reply and blocked the Tong Pass road with troops.
units.literal: Zhijun did not answer and with troops cut the Tong Pass road.

units.zh: 太祖遣劉鄩、牛存節攻知俊，知俊遂奔於茂貞，茂貞地狹，無以處之，使之西攻靈武。
units.en: Zhu Wen sent Liu Yun and Niu Cunjie against him. Zhijun fled to Maozhen, whose lands were too narrow to hold him; Maozhen sent him west against Lingwu.
units.literal: The Founder sent Liu Yun and Niu Cunjie to attack Zhijun; Zhijun then fled to Maozhen. Maozhen’s territory was narrow and he had no place to settle him, so he had him attack Lingwu in the west.

units.zh: 韓遜告急，太祖遣康懷英、寇彥卿等攻邠寧以牽之。
units.en: Han Xun cried for help. The Founder sent Kang Huaiying, Kou Yanqing, and others against Bin and Ning to tie Maozhen down.
units.literal: Han Xun reported in emergency; the Founder sent Kang Huaiying, Kou Yanqing, and others to attack Bin and Ning to pin him down.

units.zh: 知俊大敗懷英於升平，殺梁將許從實。
units.en: At Shengping Zhijun crushed Huaiying and killed the Liang general Xu Congshi.
units.literal: Zhijun at Shengping greatly defeated Huaiying and killed the Liang general Xu Congshi.

units.zh: 茂貞大喜，以知俊為涇州節度使，使攻興元，取興、鳳，圍西縣。
units.en: Maozhen rejoiced, made Zhijun governor of Jing, and sent him against Xingyuan. He took Xing and Feng and besieged Xi county.
units.literal: Maozhen was greatly pleased and made Zhijun military governor of Jingzhou, had him attack Xingyuan, took Xing and Feng, and besieged Xi county.

units.zh: 已而茂貞左右忌知俊功，以事間之，茂貞奪其軍。
units.en: Soon men at Maozhen’s ear envied Zhijun’s fame and whispered against him; Maozhen took his army away.
units.literal: Before long Maozhen’s close attendants envied Zhijun’s merit and slandered him by degrees; Maozhen stripped him of his army.

units.zh: 知俊乃奔於蜀，王建以為武信軍節度使，使返攻茂貞，取秦、鳳、階、成四州。
units.en: Zhijun fled to Shu. Wang Jian made him governor of Wuxin and sent him back against Maozhen; he took Qin, Feng, Jie, and Cheng.
units.literal: Zhijun then fled to Shu; Wang Jian made him military governor of Wuxin and had him turn back to attack Maozhen, taking Qin, Feng, Jie, and Cheng.

units.zh: 建雖待知俊甚厚，然亦陰忌其材，嘗謂左右曰：「吾老矣，吾且死，知俊非爾輩所能制，不如早圖之！」
units.en: Jian favored him lavishly yet envied his talent in secret. He told his men once: “I am old and dying. You cannot hold Zhijun—deal with him while you can!”
units.literal: Though Jian treated Zhijun very generously, he also secretly envied his talent and once told his attendants: “I am old and will soon die; Zhijun is not someone you can control—better plot against him early!”

units.zh: 而蜀人亦共嫉之。
units.en: Shu shared the envy.
units.literal: The men of Shu likewise all envied him together.

units.zh: 知俊為人色黑，而其生歲在醜。
units.en: Zhijun was dark-skinned, born in the year of the ox.
units.literal: Zhijun’s complexion was dark, and his birth year was the ox.

units.zh: 建之諸子，皆以「宗」、「承」為名，乃於裏巷構為謠言曰：「黑牛出圈棕繩斷。」
units.en: Jian’s sons all bore “Zong” or “Cheng” in their names, so alley gossip ran: “The black ox leaves the pen—the brown rope snaps.”
units.literal: Jian’s sons all used “Zong” and “Cheng” in their names, so in the lanes they fashioned a ditty: “The black ox leaves the pen—the brown rope snaps.”

units.zh: 建益惡之，遂見殺。
units.en: Jian hated him the more and had him killed.
units.literal: Jian hated him all the more and therefore had him killed.

units.zh: 丁會，字道隱，壽州壽春人也。
units.en: Ding Hui, styled Daoyin, came from Shouchun in Shou.
units.literal: Ding Hui, courtesy name Daoyin, was a native of Shouchun in Shouzhou.

units.zh: 少工挽喪之歌，尤能淒愴其聲以自喜。
units.en: As a boy he sang funeral dirges and took pride in wringing the most piercing grief from his voice.
units.literal: In youth he worked at funeral-dirge songs and especially could make his voice piercing and mournful to please himself.

units.zh: 後去為盜，與梁太祖俱從黃巢。
units.en: He left that life for the road, became a bandit, and marched with Zhu Wen under Huang Chao.
units.literal: Later he left that trade and became a bandit; he followed Huang Chao together with Liang Taizu.

units.zh: 梁太祖鎮宣武，以為宣武都押衙。
units.en: When Zhu Wen held Xuanyi he made Hui its overall adjutant.
units.literal: When Liang Taizu held Xuanyi, he made Hui overall adjutant of Xuanyi.

units.zh: 光啟四年，東都張全義襲破河陽，逐李罕之，罕之召晉兵圍河陽，全義告急。
units.en: Guangqi 4: Zhang Quanyi of the eastern capital stormed Heyang and drove out Li Hanzhi. Hanzhi called Jin to besiege the city; Quanyi cried for help.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Guangqi, Zhang Quanyi of the eastern capital raided and broke Heyang, drove out Li Hanzhi, Hanzhi called Jin troops to besiege Heyang, and Quanyi reported in emergency.

units.zh: 是時，梁軍在魏，乃遣會及葛從周等將萬人救之。
units.en: The Liang host was at Wei; they sent Hui with Ge Congzhou and ten thousand men to relieve it.
units.literal: At that time the Liang army was at Wei; they therefore sent Hui with Ge Congzhou and others leading ten thousand men to rescue it.

units.zh: 會等行至河陰，謀曰：「罕之料吾不敢渡九鼎，以吾兵少而來遠，且不虞吾之速至也。
units.en: At Heyin Hui and the others plotted: “Hanzhi thinks we will not cross the Jiuding—few men, a long march, and he will not expect us so soon.
units.literal: When Hui and the rest reached Heyin they plotted: “Hanzhi reckons we dare not cross the Jiuding—our troops are few and we have come from far, and he will not expect us to arrive so fast.

units.zh: 出其不意，掩其不備者，兵家之勝策也。」
units.en: Hit what he does not expect, catch him unready—that is how battles are won.”
units.literal: To strike where the enemy does not expect and catch him unprepared—that is the strategist’s winning move.”

units.zh: 乃渡九鼎，直趨河陽，戰於沇水，罕之大敗，河陽圍解。
units.en: They crossed, raced on Heyang, fought at the Yan River, broke Hanzhi completely, and lifted the siege.
units.literal: They then crossed the Jiuding, drove straight on Heyang, fought at the Yan River, and Hanzhi was utterly defeated; the Heyang siege was lifted.

units.zh: 大順元年，梁軍擊魏，會及葛從周破黎陽、臨河，遂敗羅弘信於內黃。
units.en: Dashun 1: Liang struck Wei. Hui and Ge Congzhou took Liyang and Linhe and at Neihuang beat Luo Hongxin.
units.literal: In the first year of Dashun the Liang army struck Wei; Hui and Ge Congzhou took Liyang and Linhe and at Neihuang defeated Luo Hongxin.

units.zh: 梁軍攻時溥於徐州，遣會別攻宿州，刺史張筠閉城距守，會堰汴水浸其東，城壞，筠降。
units.en: Liang besieged Shi Pu at Xu and sent Hui against Su. Prefect Zhang Yun barred the gates. Hui dammed the Bian to flood the east wall; the wall gave way and Yun surrendered.
units.literal: The Liang army attacked Shi Pu at Xuzhou and sent Hui separately to attack Suzhou; prefect Zhang Yun shut the city and held out. Hui dammed the Bian River to flood its east wall; the wall collapsed and Yun surrendered.

units.zh: 兗州朱瑾以兵萬餘擊單父，會及瑾戰於金鄉，大敗之。
units.en: Zhu Jin of Yan brought ten thousand men against Shanfu; Hui met him at Jinxiang and broke him.
units.literal: Zhu Jin of Yanzhou led more than ten thousand men to strike Shanfu; Hui fought Jin at Jinxiang and utterly defeated him.

units.zh: 光化二年，李罕之叛晉，以潞州降梁。
units.en: Guanghua 2: Li Hanzhi turned on Jin and gave Luzhou to Liang.
units.literal: In the second year of Guanghua, Li Hanzhi rebelled against Jin and surrendered Luzhou to Liang.

units.zh: 會自河陽攻晉澤州，下之。
units.en: From Heyang Hui struck Jin’s Ze and took it.
units.literal: Hui from Heyang attacked Jin’s Ze prefecture and took it.

units.zh: 乃以會為昭義軍留後，會畏梁太祖雄猜，常稱疾者累年。
units.en: He was made acting commissioner of Zhaoyi. Hui feared Zhu Wen’s suspicion and for years pleaded sickness.
units.literal: He was then made acting commissioner of Zhaoyi; Hui feared Liang Taizu’s fierce suspicion and for years often claimed illness.

units.zh: 天復元年，太祖復起會為昭義軍節度使。
units.en: Tianfu 1: the Founder restored him as military governor of Zhaoyi.
units.literal: In the first year of Tianfu the Founder again raised Hui to military governor of Zhaoyi.

units.zh: 昭宗遇弒，會與三軍縞素髮哀。
units.en: When Zhaozong was murdered, Hui and the host went into white hemp and loose hair for mourning.
units.literal: When Zhaozong met assassination, Hui with the three armies wore white hemp and let their hair hang in mourning.

units.zh: 梁軍攻燕滄州，燕王守光乞師於晉，晉人為攻潞州，會乃降晉。
units.en: Liang besieged Yan at Cangzhou; Shouguang begged Jin for help; Jin struck Luzhou in answer, and Hui went over to Jin.
units.literal: The Liang army attacked Yan at Cangzhou; Yan’s King Shouguang begged troops from Jin, and Jin men attacked Luzhou in turn, so Hui surrendered to Jin.

units.zh: 晉王以會歸於太原，賜以甲第，位在諸將上。
units.en: The Prince of Jin brought him to Taiyuan, gave him a grand house, and set him above the other generals.
units.literal: The Prince of Jin brought Hui back to Taiyuan, bestowed a fine mansion, and ranked him above the other generals.

units.zh: 莊宗立，以會為都招討使。
units.en: When Zhuangzong rose he made Hui overall pacification commissioner.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he made Hui overall pacification commissioner.

units.zh: 天祐七年，以疾卒於太原。
units.en: Tianyou 7 he died of illness at Taiyuan.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Tianyou he died of illness at Taiyuan.

units.zh: 唐興，追贈太師。
units.en: When Tang rose he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: When Tang rose he was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 賀德倫
units.en: He Delun
units.literal: He Delun

units.zh: 賀德倫，河西人也。
units.en: He Delun came from Hexi.
units.literal: He Delun was a man of Hexi.

units.zh: 少為滑州牙將。
units.en: As a youth he was a tooth officer at Huazhou.
units.literal: In youth he served as a tooth officer at Huazhou.

units.zh: 梁太祖兼領宣義，德倫從太祖征伐，以功累遷平盧軍節度使。
units.en: When Zhu Wen also held Xuanyi, Delun followed him on campaign and rose by stages to military governor of Pinglu.
units.literal: When Liang Taizu also held Xuanyi, Delun followed the Founder on campaign and by merit was repeatedly promoted to military governor of the Pinglu army.

units.zh: 貞明元年，魏州楊師厚卒，末帝以魏兵素驕難制，乃分相、澶、衞三州建昭德軍，以張筠為節度使；
units.en: Zhenming 1: Yang Shihou of Wei died. The Last Emperor, finding Wei troops proud and unruly, carved out Xiang, Chan, and Wei for a new Zhaode command under Zhang Yun;
units.literal: In the first year of Zhenming, Yang Shihou of Weizhou died. The Last Emperor, because Wei troops were habitually arrogant and hard to control, split off Xiang, Cao, and Wei prefectures to establish the Zhaode army and made Zhang Jun its military governor;

units.zh: 魏、博、貝三州仍為天雄軍，以德倫為節度使。
units.en: Wei, Bo, and Bei stayed Tianxiong, with Delun as governor.
units.literal: Wei, Bo, and Bei prefectures remained the Tianxiong army, with Delun as military governor.

units.zh: 遣劉鄩以兵六萬渡河，聲言攻鎮定，王彥章以騎兵五百入魏州，屯金波亭以虞變；
units.en: He sent Liu Yun with sixty thousand men across the river, feigning a strike on Zhen and Ding, while Wang Yanzhang entered Wei with five hundred horse and camped at Jinbo Pavilion to watch for trouble;
units.literal: He sent Liu Yun with sixty thousand men across the river, proclaiming an attack on Zhen and Ding, while Wang Yanzhang entered Weizhou with five hundred cavalry and encamped at Jinbo Pavilion to guard against trouble;

units.zh: 分魏牙兵之半入昭德。
units.en: Half the Wei tooth troops were sent into Zhaode.
units.literal: He sent half the Wei tooth troops into Zhaode.

units.zh: 租庸使遣孔目吏閱魏兵籍，檢校府庫。
units.en: The rent-and-corvée commissioner sent clerks to audit Wei troop rolls and inspect the treasury.
units.literal: The commissioner of rents and labor corvée sent clerks to review Wei troop rosters and inspect the treasury.

units.zh: 德倫促牙兵上道，牙兵親戚相訣別，哭聲盈塗。
units.en: Delun pressed the tooth troops to march. Kinsmen took tearful leave along the road, and weeping filled the streets.
units.literal: Delun urged the tooth troops onto the road; kinsmen of the tooth troops took tearful farewells, and weeping filled the streets.

units.zh: 効節軍將張彥謀於其眾曰：「朝廷以我軍府彊盛，設法殘破之。
units.en: Zhang Yan, general of the Xiaojie army, plotted with his men: "The court sees our district too strong and means to break us.
units.literal: Zhang Yan, general of the Xiaojie army, plotted before his followers and said: "The court, because our army district is strong and mighty, has devised means to break it apart.

units.zh: 況我六州舊為藩府，未嘗遠出河門，一旦離親戚，去鄉里，生不如死。」
units.en: Our six prefectures were a frontier command; we never marched far beyond the He Gate. To leave kin and home at once—better dead than alive."
units.literal: Moreover, our six prefectures were formerly a frontier commandery; we have never marched far beyond the He Gate. To leave kinsmen and homeland at a stroke—death is better than life."

units.zh: 乃相與夜攻金波亭，彥章走出。
units.en: That night they stormed Jinbo Pavilion together, and Yanzhang fled.
units.literal: They then together attacked Jinbo Pavilion by night, and Yanzhang fled.

units.zh: 遲明，魏兵攻牙城，殺五百餘人，執德倫致之樓上，縱兵大掠。
units.en: At dawn Wei troops stormed the barracks city, killed more than five hundred men, seized Delun and hauled him to the tower, and let the army loot at will.
units.literal: At dawn Wei troops attacked the barracks city, killed more than five hundred men, seized Delun and brought him up to the tower, and let the soldiers plunder freely.

units.zh: 末帝遣供奉官扈異馳至魏諭彥，許以刺史。
units.en: Liang’s Last Emperor sent Hu Yi racing to Wei to reason with Zhang Yan and promised him a prefecture.
units.literal: The Last Emperor sent palace supply officer Hu Yi in haste to Wei to instruct Yan and promised him a prefecture.

units.zh: 彥謂異曰：「為我報皇帝，三軍不負朝廷，朝廷負三軍，割隸無名，所以亂耳。
units.en: Yan told Yi: “Tell the Emperor for me: the army has not failed the court—the court failed the army. Carving away our districts without cause is what bred this chaos.
units.literal: Yan said to Yi: “Report to the Emperor for me: the three armies have not failed the court—the court has failed the three armies. Cutting off our districts without cause is why there is disorder.

units.zh: 但以六州還魏，而詔劉鄩反兵，皇帝可以高枕。」
units.en: Give the six prefectures back to Wei and recall Liu Yun, and the Emperor can sleep easy.”
units.literal: Only return the six prefectures to Wei and order Liu Yun to turn his army back, and the Emperor may sleep easy.”

units.zh: 異還，言彥狂蹶不足畏，宜促鄩兵擊之。
units.en: Yi came back and said Yan was a mad rebel, nothing to fear—push Liu Yun to strike.
units.literal: Yi returned and said Yan was wildly insolent and not worth fearing; Liu Yun’s troops should be urged to strike him.

units.zh: 末帝使人諭彥，以制置已定，不可復易。
units.en: The Last Emperor sent word: the arrangement was set and would not change.
units.literal: The Last Emperor sent men to instruct Yan that the disposition was already fixed and could not be changed again.

units.zh: 使者三反，彥怒曰：「傭保兒敢如是邪！」
units.en: Three times the envoy returned; Yan raged: “Does this hired lackey dare talk so!”
units.literal: The envoy came back three times; Yan raged: “Does this hired hand dare act so!”

units.zh: 乃召羅紹威故吏司空颋曰：「為我作奏，若復依違，則渡河虜之耳！」
units.en: He called Luo Shaowei’s old clerk Sikong Ting: “Write my memorial—if they keep stalling, I will cross the river and make captives of them!”
units.literal: He then summoned Luo Shaowei’s former clerk Sikong Ting and said: “Draft a memorial for me—if they keep wavering, I will cross the river and take them as captives!”

units.zh: 末帝優詔答之，言：「王镕死，鎮人請降，遣鄩以兵定鎮州，非有佗也，若魏不便之，即召鄩還。」
units.en: The Last Emperor answered gently: “Wang Rong is dead; Zhen asks to submit; I sent Liu Yun to settle it—nothing more. If Wei is uneasy, I will recall him.”
units.literal: The Last Emperor answered with a soothing edict, saying: “Wang Rong is dead; the men of the garrison beg to surrender; I sent Liu Yun with troops to settle Zhenzhou—there is nothing else. If Wei finds it inconvenient, I will recall Yun at once.”

units.zh: 戒彥勿為朝廷生事。
units.en: He warned Yan not to stir trouble for the court.
units.literal: He warned Yan not to make trouble for the court.

units.zh: 彥乃以楊師厚鎮魏州嘗帶招討使，逼德倫論列之，末帝不許，諭以詔書，彥裂詔書抵於地，曰：「愚主聽人穿鼻，難與共事矣！」
units.en: Yan cited Yang Shihou’s old joint title as pacification commissioner at Wei and made Delun argue it in memorials. The Last Emperor refused and sent an edict; Yan tore it and flung it down: “A fool led by the nose—no man can serve him!”
units.literal: Yan then cited that when Yang Shihou held Weizhou he had also borne the pacification commissioner title, forced Delun to argue the point in memorials, and the Last Emperor would not agree but instructed him by edict; Yan tore the edict and threw it to the ground, saying: “A foolish ruler lets men lead him by the nose—hard to serve him any longer!”

units.zh: 乃迫德倫降晉，德倫惶恐曰：「惟將軍命。」
units.en: He forced Delun to surrender to Jin. Delun quaked: “Only as the general commands.”
units.literal: He then forced Delun to surrender to Jin; Delun said in terror: “Only as the general commands.”

units.zh: 乃遣牙將曹廷隱奉書莊宗。
units.en: Then he sent tooth officer Cao Tingyin with a letter to Zhuangzong.
units.literal: Then he sent tooth officer Cao Tingyin with a letter to Zhuangzong.

units.zh: 莊宗入魏，德倫以彥逼己，遣人陰訴於莊宗，莊宗斬彥於臨清而後入。
units.en: When Zhuangzong entered Wei, Delun—pressed by Yan—sent secret word to the throne. Zhuangzong beheaded Yan at Linqing, then marched in.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Wei, Delun because Yan had coerced him sent men in secret to complain to Zhuangzong; Zhuangzong beheaded Yan at Linqing and only then entered.

units.zh: 徙德倫為大同軍節度使。
units.en: Delun was moved to military governor of Datong.
units.literal: Delun was transferred to military governor of Datong.

units.zh: 行至太原，監軍張承業留之。
units.en: At Taiyuan Inspector Zhang Chengye held him back.
units.literal: When he reached Taiyuan, military inspector Zhang Chengye detained him.

units.zh: 王檀攻太原，德倫麾下多奔檀，承業懼德倫為變，殺之。
units.en: Wang Tan struck Taiyuan; Delun’s men ran to Tan. Chengye feared revolt and killed Delun.
units.literal: Wang Tan attacked Taiyuan; many of Delun’s followers fled to Tan; Chengye feared Delun would turn traitor and killed him.

units.zh: 閻寶，字瓊美，鄆州人也。
units.en: Yan Bao, styled Qiongmei, came from Yun.
units.literal: Yan Bao, courtesy name Qiongmei, was a native of Yunzhou.

units.zh: 少為朱瑾牙將，瑾走淮南，寶降於梁。
units.en: As a youth he served Zhu Jin; when Jin fled to Huainan, Bao came over to Liang.
units.literal: In youth he was a tooth officer under Zhu Jin; when Jin fled to Huainan, Bao surrendered to Liang.

units.zh: 梁太祖時，為諸軍都虞候，常從諸將征伐，未嘗獨立戰功。
units.en: Under Zhu Wen he was overall adjutant of the armies, always on campaign with the host, never winning credit alone.
units.literal: Under Liang Taizu he was overall adjutant of the armies and constantly followed the generals on campaign, never winning merit on his own.

units.zh: 至末帝時，以寶為保義軍節度使。
units.en: Under the Last Emperor he became military governor of Baoyi.
units.literal: By the time of the Last Emperor he made Bao military governor of Baoyi.

units.zh: 貞明三年，賀德倫以魏博降晉，晉軍攻下洺、磁、相、衛，移兵圍邢州。
units.en: Zhenming 3: He Delun gave Weibo to Jin. Jin took Ming, Ci, Xiang, and Wei and moved to besiege Xing.
units.literal: In the third year of Zhenming, He Delun surrendered Weibo to Jin; Jin troops took Ming, Ci, Xiang, and Wei and shifted their army to besiege Xingzhou.

units.zh: 末帝遣捉生都指揮使張溫將五百騎救寶，溫至內黃，遇晉軍，乃降晉。
units.en: The Last Emperor sent Zhang Wen of the prisoner-catching guard with five hundred horse to relieve Bao. At Neihuang Wen met Jin and went over.
units.literal: The Last Emperor sent prisoner-catching overall commander Zhang Wen with five hundred cavalry to rescue Bao; Wen reached Neihuang, met Jin troops, and surrendered to Jin.

units.zh: 晉遣溫將所降梁軍至城下招寶，寶遂降晉。
units.en: Jin sent Wen with the surrendered Liang men to call Bao from the wall; Bao came over.
units.literal: Jin sent Wen to lead the surrendered Liang troops below the walls to summon Bao, and Bao then surrendered to Jin.

units.zh: 晉王拜寶檢校太尉、同中書門下平章事，領天平軍節度使、東南面招討使，位在諸將上。
units.en: The Prince of Jin made him acting Grand Mentor and Secretariat co-equal, military governor of Tianping and southeastern-route pacifier, set above the other generals.
units.literal: The Prince of Jin appointed Bao acting Grand Mentor and co-equal with the Secretariat, holding the titles of military governor of Tianping and southeastern-route pacification commissioner, ranked above the other generals.

units.zh: 梁、晉戰胡柳，晉軍敗。
units.en: Liang and Jin met at Huliu; Jin lost.
units.literal: Liang and Jin fought at Huliu; the Jin army was defeated.

units.zh: 莊宗欲引兵退保臨濮，寶曰：「夫決勝料勢，決戰料情，情勢既得，斷在不疑。
units.en: Zhuangzong meant to pull back to Linpu. Bao said: “Victory is momentum; battle is spirit. Once you have both, strike without hesitation.
units.literal: Zhuangzong wished to withdraw the army to hold Linpu; Bao said: “To decide victory one weighs momentum; to decide battle one weighs spirit—once momentum and spirit are gained, the cut must be made without doubt.

units.zh: 今梁兵窘蹙，其勢可破；
units.en: Liang is cornered; their line can be broken;
units.literal: Now Liang troops are cornered and their momentum can be broken;

units.zh: 勝而驕怠，其情可知。
units.en: they have won and grown proud and slack—their spirit tells you so.
units.literal: having won they are proud and slack—their spirit can be read.

units.zh: 此不可失之時也。」
units.en: This is the moment not to waste.”
units.literal: This is a moment that must not be lost.”

units.zh: 莊宗謝曰：「微公，幾敗吾事。」
units.en: Zhuangzong thanked him: “Without you I would have ruined everything.”
units.literal: Zhuangzong thanked him: “Without you, I would nearly have ruined the affair.”

units.zh: 乃整軍復戰，遂敗梁兵。
units.en: He reformed the line, fought again, and broke Liang completely.
units.literal: He then reformed the army and fought again, and utterly defeated the Liang army.

units.zh: 十八年，晉軍討張文禮於鎮州，以寶為招討使。
units.en: Year 18 the Jin host campaigned against Zhang Wenli at Zhen and made Bao pacification commissioner.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year the Jin army campaigned against Zhang Wenli at Zhenzhou and made Bao pacification commissioner.

units.zh: 明年三月，寶戰敗，退保趙州。
units.en: Next year, third month, he lost a battle and fell back to Zhao.
units.literal: In the third month of the next year Bao was defeated in battle and withdrew to hold Zhao prefecture.

units.zh: 慚憤發疽卒，追贈太師。
units.en: Shame and rage brought boils; he died. They posthumously made him Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: Ashamed and enraged, he broke out in boils and died; he was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 晉天福中，追封太原王。
units.en: Under Jin’s Tianfu era he was posthumously made Prince of Taiyuan.
units.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin he was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Taiyuan.

units.zh: 康延孝
units.en: Kang Yanxiao
units.literal: Kang Yanxiao

units.zh: 康延孝，代北人也。
units.en: Kang Yanxiao came from the northern frontier.
units.literal: Kang Yanxiao was a man of the northern frontier.

units.zh: 為太原軍卒，有罪亡命於梁。
units.en: He served in the Taiyuan army; guilty of a crime he fled to Liang.
units.literal: He was a soldier of the Taiyuan army; guilty of a crime he fled his life to Liang.

units.zh: 末帝遣段凝軍於河上，以延孝為左右先鋒指揮使。
units.en: The Last Emperor put Duan Ning on the river with an army and made Yanxiao commander of the left and right vanguard.
units.literal: The Last Emperor sent Duan Ning with an army on the river; he made Yanxiao commander of the left and right vanguard.

units.zh: 延孝見梁末帝任用群小，知其必亡，乃以百騎奔於唐。
units.en: Yanxiao saw the Last Emperor trusting petty men and knew Liang must fall; he rode to Tang with a hundred horse.
units.literal: Yanxiao saw Liang’s Last Emperor employing petty men and knew it must perish; he therefore fled to Tang with a hundred horsemen.

units.zh: 見莊宗於朝城，莊宗解禦衣、金帶以賜之。
units.en: He met Zhuangzong at Chaocheng; Zhuangzong stripped off his own imperial robe and gold belt and gave them to him.
units.literal: He met Zhuangzong at Chaocheng; Zhuangzong removed his own imperial robe and gold belt and bestowed them on him.

units.zh: 拜延孝博州刺史、捧日軍使兼南面招討指揮使。
units.en: He made Yanxiao prefect of Bo, commander of the Sun-Raising Army, and southern-route pacification commander.
units.literal: He appointed Yanxiao prefect of Bo, commander of the Sun-Raising Army, and also southern-route pacification commander.

units.zh: 莊宗屏人問延孝梁事，延孝具言：「末帝懦弱。
units.en: Zhuangzong sent the room away and asked about Liang. Yanxiao told him plainly: “The Last Emperor is weak.
units.literal: Zhuangzong dismissed the room and questioned Yanxiao on Liang affairs; Yanxiao laid them out fully: “The Last Emperor is weak.

units.zh: 趙巖婿也，張漢傑婦家，皆用事。
units.en: Zhao Yan is his son-in-law; Zhang Hanjie is his wife’s people—both rule.
units.literal: Zhao Yan is his son-in-law; Zhang Hanjie is his wife’s kin—both hold power.

units.zh: 段凝奸邪，以入金多為大將，自其父時故將皆出其下。
units.en: Duan Ning is treacherous; he bought rank with gold and sits above every general who served his father.
units.literal: Duan Ning is treacherous and wicked; because he paid the most gold he became a great general, and all the old generals from his father’s day rank below him.

units.zh: 王彥章，驍將也，遣漢傑監其軍而制之。
units.en: Wang Yanzhang is a fierce fighter, yet Hanjie was sent to watch his army and hold him back.
units.literal: Wang Yanzhang is a fierce general, yet Hanjie was sent to supervise his army and restrain him.

units.zh: 小人進任，而忠臣勇士皆見疏斥，此其必亡之勢也。」
units.en: Petty men take office while loyal ministers and brave warriors are pushed aside—that is the shape of a state doomed to fall.”
units.literal: Petty men are advanced to office while loyal ministers and brave warriors are all kept distant and cast aside—this is the momentum of certain ruin.”

units.zh: 莊宗又問梁計如何，曰：「臣在梁時，竊聞其議：期以仲冬大舉，遣董璋以陜虢、澤潞之眾出石會以攻太原；
units.en: Zhuangzong asked what Liang intended next. Yanxiao said: “In Liang I heard them plan a winter offensive—Dong Zhang with Shaan-Guo and Ze-Lu troops through Shihui Pass on Taiyuan;
units.literal: Zhuangzong again asked what Liang’s plan was. He said: “When I was in Liang I overheard their councils: they set a great campaign for mid-winter, to send Dong Zhang with the forces of Shaan-Guo and Ze-Lu out Shihui Pass against Taiyuan;

units.zh: 霍彥威以關西、汝、洛之兵掠邢洺以趨鎮定；
units.en: Huo Yanwei with Guanxi, Ru, and Luo forces to sweep Xing and Mo and drive on Zhen and Ding;
units.literal: Huo Yanwei with Guanxi, Ru, and Luo troops to raid Xing and Mo and press toward Zhen and Ding;

units.zh: 王彥章以京師禁衛擊鄆州；
units.en: Wang Yanzhang with the capital guard against Yanzhou;
units.literal: Wang Yanzhang with the capital guard to strike Yanzhou;

units.zh: 段凝以河上之軍當陛下。」
units.en: Duan Ning with the river army to hold Your Majesty.”
units.literal: Duan Ning with the river army to face Your Majesty.”

units.zh: 莊宗初聞延孝言梁必亡，喜，及聞其大舉也，懼，曰：「其將何以禦之？」
units.en: At first Zhuangzong rejoiced to hear Liang was finished; when he heard of the grand plan he grew afraid. “How do we answer this?”
units.literal: At first, hearing Yanxiao say Liang must perish, Zhuangzong was pleased; when he heard of this great campaign he was afraid and said: “How shall we meet it?”

units.zh: 延孝曰：「梁兵雖眾，分則無餘。
units.en: Yanxiao said: “Liang may field a host, but split it and each piece is thin.
units.literal: Yanxiao said: “Though Liang’s troops are many, once divided they have no surplus.

units.zh: 臣請待其既分，以鐵騎五千自鄆趨汴，出其不意，搗其空虛，不旬日，天下定矣。」
units.en: Let them divide first. Give me five thousand iron horsemen from Yan straight to Bian, catch them empty, and within ten days the realm is ours.”
units.literal: I ask to wait until they have divided, then with five thousand iron cavalry ride from Yan to Bian, take them unawares, and strike their emptiness—in less than ten days the realm will be settled.”

units.zh: 莊宗甚壯其言。
units.en: Zhuangzong took fire from the plan.
units.literal: Zhuangzong was greatly heartened by his words.

units.zh: 後董璋等雖不出兵，而梁兵悉屬段凝於河上，京師無備，莊宗卒用延孝策，自鄆入汴，凡八日而滅梁。
units.en: Dong Zhang never marched, but every Liang soldier on the river went to Duan Ning and the capital stood bare. Zhuangzong took Yanxiao’s counsel, rode from Yan into Bian, and in eight days Liang was gone.
units.literal: Later, though Dong Zhang and the others did not march out, all Liang troops on the river were placed under Duan Ning; the capital was undefended. Zhuangzong at last used Yanxiao’s plan, entered Bian from Yan, and in eight days Liang was destroyed.

units.zh: 以功拜鄭州防禦使，賜姓名曰李紹琛。
units.en: For the deed he was made Zhengzhou defense commissioner and renamed Li Shaochen.
units.literal: For merit he was made defense commissioner of Zhengzhou and granted the surname and name Li Shaochen.

units.zh: 二年，遷保義軍節度使。
units.en: In the second year he was moved to military governor of Baoyi.
units.literal: In the second year he was transferred to military governor of the Baoyi army.

units.zh: 三年，征蜀，以延孝為先鋒排陣斬斫使，破鳳州，取固鎮，降興州。
units.en: In the third year, on the Shu campaign, Yanxiao was named vanguard array-cutting commissioner. He stormed Feng, seized Guzhen, and took Xing’s surrender.
units.literal: In the third year, on the campaign against Shu, Yanxiao was made vanguard array-cutting execution commissioner; he broke Feng Prefecture, took Guzhen, and received the surrender of Xing Prefecture.

units.zh: 與王衍戰三泉，衍敗走，斷吉柏江浮橋，延孝造舟以渡，進取綿州。
units.en: He met Wang Yan at Sanquan and broke him. Yan fled, cut the Jibo floating bridge, and Yanxiao built boats to cross and push on Mian.
units.literal: He fought Wang Yan at Sanquan; Yan was defeated and fled. Yan cut the Jibo River floating bridge. Yanxiao built boats to cross and advanced to take Mian Prefecture.

units.zh: 衍復斷綿江浮橋。
units.en: Yan cut the Mian bridge as well.
units.literal: Yan again cut the Mian River floating bridge.

units.zh: 延孝謂招撫使李嚴曰：「吾遠軍千里，入人之國，利在速戰。
units.en: Yanxiao told Pacification Commissioner Li Yan: “We are a thousand li from home in another man’s land. Speed is everything.
units.literal: Yanxiao said to Pacification Commissioner Li Yan: “My army has come a thousand li into another man’s country; the gain lies in swift battle.

units.zh: 乘衍破膽之時，但得百騎過鹿頭關，彼將迎降不暇。
units.en: Strike while Yan’s nerve is broken. A hundred riders through Lutou Pass and he will not even have time to kneel.
units.literal: While Yan still reels from defeat, let a hundred horsemen pass Lutou Pass and he will have no time to receive surrender.

units.zh: 若修繕橋梁，必留數日，使衍得閉關為備，則勝負未可知也。」
units.en: Repair bridges and we lose days; Yan will bar the passes and the fight becomes anyone’s guess.”
units.literal: If we repair bridges we must linger days and let Yan shut the passes and prepare—then victory and defeat cannot be known.”

units.zh: 因與嚴乘馬浮江，軍士隨之濟者千餘人，遂入鹿頭關，下漢州，居三日，後軍始至。
units.en: He and Yan forded the river on horseback; a thousand men swam after them. They took Lutou Pass and Han, camped three days, and only then did the main body come up.
units.literal: He and Yan therefore rode their horses across the river; more than a thousand soldiers followed them across. They entered Lutou Pass, took Han Prefecture, and waited three days before the rear army arrived.

units.zh: 衍弟宗弼果以蜀降。
units.en: Yan’s brother Zongbi surrendered Shu.
units.literal: Yan’s younger brother Zongbi indeed surrendered Shu.

units.zh: 延孝屯漢州，以俟魏王繼岌。
units.en: Yanxiao held Han and waited for the Prince of Wei, Jiji.
units.literal: Yanxiao encamped at Han Prefecture to await the Prince of Wei, Jiji.

units.zh: 蜀平，延孝功為多。
units.en: When Shu fell, no one’s share of the credit matched Yanxiao’s.
units.literal: When Shu was pacified, Yanxiao’s merit was greatest.

units.zh: 左廂馬步軍都指揮使董璋位在延孝下，然特見重於郭崇韜。
units.en: Dong Zhang of the Left Wing horse and foot stood beneath Yanxiao in rank, yet Guo Chongtao singled him out.
units.literal: Dong Zhang, commander of the Left Wing horse and foot, ranked below Yanxiao, yet was especially favored by Guo Chongtao.

units.zh: 崇韜有軍事，獨召璋與計議，而不問延孝，延孝大怒，責璋曰：「吾有平蜀之功，公等仆遬相從，反俯首郭公之門，吾為都將，獨不能以軍法斬公邪？」
units.en: Chongtao called Zhang alone to war councils and passed Yanxiao by. Yanxiao raged at Zhang: “I pacified Shu. You scurried in my train, then crawled to Guo’s door. I command this army—shall I not cut you down by martial law?”
units.literal: When Chongtao had military business he summoned Zhang alone to counsel and did not consult Yanxiao. Yanxiao was furious and rebuked Zhang: “I have the merit of pacifying Shu. You all trailed in my train, yet now bow your heads at Lord Guo’s gate. I am commander-in-chief—can I alone not execute you by military law?”

units.zh: 璋訴於崇韜，崇韜解璋軍職，表為東川節度使，延孝愈怒曰：「吾冒白刃，犯險阻，以定兩川，璋有何功而得旄節！」
units.en: Zhang ran to Chongtao. Chongtao stripped his command and made him Dongchuan military governor. Yanxiao fumed: “I took the blade and the cliff to win the two rivers—what did Zhang do to earn a command flag?”
units.literal: Zhang appealed to Chongtao. Chongtao relieved Zhang of command and memorialized him as military governor of Dongchuan. Yanxiao grew angrier and said: “I braved the blade and the pass to settle the two rivers—what merit has Zhang to win a command flag!”

units.zh: 因見崇韜言其不可。
units.en: He went to Chongtao and said the appointment was wrong.
units.literal: He then saw Chongtao and told him it could not stand.

units.zh: 崇韜曰：「紹琛反邪？
units.en: Chongtao said: “Does Shaochen mean to rebel?
units.literal: Chongtao said: “Does Shaochen rebel?

units.zh: 敢違吾節度！」
units.en: He dares defy my authority!”
units.literal: He dares defy my command!”

units.zh: 延孝懼而退。
units.en: Yanxiao backed away in fear.
units.literal: Yanxiao feared him and withdrew.

units.zh: 明年崇韜死，延孝謂璋曰：「公復俯首何門邪？」
units.en: The next year Chongtao was dead. Yanxiao asked Zhang: “Whose threshold do you crawl to now?”
units.literal: The next year Chongtao died. Yanxiao said to Zhang: “At whose door will you bow your head now?”

units.zh: 璋求哀以免。
units.en: Zhang pleaded and was let off.
units.literal: Zhang begged for mercy and was spared.

units.zh: 繼岌班師，命延孝以萬二千人為殿，行至武連，聞朱友謙無罪見殺。
units.en: Jiji marched east and left Yanxiao twelve thousand men as rearguard. At Wulian came word that Zhu Youqian, though innocent, had been put to death.
units.literal: Jiji led the army home and ordered Yanxiao with twelve thousand men as rearguard. When they reached Wulian they heard Zhu Youqian had been killed though guiltless.

units.zh: 友謙有子令德在遂州，莊宗遣使者詔繼岌即誅之。
units.en: Youqian’s son Lingde was at Suizhou. Zhuangzong sent orders for Jiji to kill him on the spot.
units.literal: Youqian had a son, Lingde, at Suizhou. Zhuangzong sent an envoy ordering Jiji to execute him at once.

units.zh: 繼岌不遣延孝，而遣董璋，延孝已自疑，及璋過延孝軍，又不謁，延孝大怒，謂其下曰：「南平梁，西取蜀，其謀盡出於郭公，而汗馬之勞，攻城破敵者我也。
units.en: Jiji sent Zhang, not Yanxiao. Yanxiao was already uneasy; Zhang passed his camp without a visit and Yanxiao exploded to his officers: “The south broke Liang and the west took Shu on Guo’s maps, but the marching and the breaches were mine.
units.literal: Jiji did not send Yanxiao but sent Dong Zhang. Yanxiao was already suspicious; when Zhang passed Yanxiao’s camp and did not call on him, Yanxiao was furious and said to his men: “To break Liang in the south and take Shu in the west—the plans all came from Lord Guo, yet the sweat of the march and the storming of walls were mine.

units.zh: 今郭公已死，我豈得存？
units.en: Guo is dead. How do I live?
units.literal: Now Lord Guo is dead—how can I survive?

units.zh: 而友謙與我俱背梁以歸唐者，友謙之禍次及我矣！」
units.en: Youqian and I both fled Liang for Tang. His slaughter comes for me next!”
units.literal: Youqian and I alike left Liang and came to Tang. Youqian’s calamity will reach me next!”

units.zh: 延孝部下皆友謙舊將，知友謙被族，皆號哭訴於軍門曰：「朱公無罪，二百口被誅，舊將往往從死，我等死必矣！」
units.en: Yanxiao’s men were Youqian’s old captains. Learning the clan was wiped out, they wailed at the gate: “Zhu was innocent—two hundred lives—and his veterans died with him. We are next!”
units.literal: Yanxiao’s subordinates were all Youqian’s old officers. Knowing Youqian’s clan had been exterminated, they wept at the camp gate: “Lord Zhu was guiltless, yet two hundred mouths were killed. Old officers often died with him. We too are dead men!”

units.zh: 延孝遂擁其眾自劍州返入蜀，自稱西川節度、三川制置等使。
units.en: Yanxiao turned his host from Jian back into Shu and called himself Xichuan military governor and Three Rivers commissioner.
units.literal: Yanxiao therefore led his troops back from Jian Prefecture into Shu, styling himself military governor of Xichuan and commissioner for the Three Rivers and the rest.

units.zh: 馳檄蜀人，數日之間，眾至五萬。
units.en: His proclamations ran through Shu; in days he had fifty thousand men.
units.literal: He sent proclamations through Shu; within days his force reached fifty thousand.

units.zh: 繼岌遣任圜以七千騎追之，及於漢州，會孟知祥夾攻之，延孝戰敗，被擒，載以檻車。
units.en: Jiji sent Ren Yuan with seven thousand horse. At Han, Meng Zhixiang closed the other jaw. Yanxiao lost, was taken, and hauled away in a cage-cart.
units.literal: Jiji sent Ren Yuan with seven thousand cavalry in pursuit. At Han Prefecture they joined Meng Zhixiang in a pincer; Yanxiao was defeated, captured, and loaded into a caged cart.

units.zh: 圜置酒軍中，引檻車至坐上，知祥酌大卮從車中飲之而謂曰：「公自梁朝脫身歸命，遂擁節旄。
units.en: Yuan feasted the army and had the cage-cart drawn to his seat. Zhixiang filled a great cup, drank with the prisoner, and said: “You slipped out of Liang and gave yourself to Tang, and soon you wore a command flag.
units.literal: Yuan set wine in camp and had the cage-cart brought before his seat. Zhixiang poured a great cup, drank with him from the cart, and said: “You left the Liang court and came to allegiance, and soon held a command flag.

units.zh: 今平蜀之功，何患富貴，而入此檻車邪？」
units.en: Shu is won. What lack of honor could drive you into a cage?”
units.literal: Now with the merit of pacifying Shu, what fear of wealth and rank—why enter this cage-cart?”

units.zh: 延孝曰：「郭崇韜佐命之臣，功在第一，兵不血刃而取兩川，一旦無罪，闔門受戮。
units.en: Yanxiao said: “Chongtao was the emperor’s right hand; his merit stood first. He took both rivers without staining a blade—then, innocent, his whole house was cut down in a day.
units.literal: Yanxiao said: “Guo Chongtao was a minister who aided the Mandate; his merit ranked first. Without a drop of blood he took the two rivers—then in a day, guiltless, his whole house was slaughtered.

units.zh: 顧如延孝，何保首領。
units.en: What hope had a man like me of keeping his head?
units.literal: As for one like Yanxiao, how could he keep his head?

units.zh: 以此不敢歸朝耳！」
units.en: That is why I would not go back to court!”
units.literal: For that I dared not return to court!”

units.zh: 任圜東還，延孝檻車至鳳翔，莊宗遣宦者殺之。
units.en: Ren Yuan marched east. The cage-cart reached Fengxiang; Zhuangzong sent a eunuch to kill him.
units.literal: Ren Yuan marched east. Yanxiao’s cage-cart reached Fengxiang, and Zhuangzong sent a eunuch to kill him.
